level1.title: 1st Level (Clinic / Local Hospital)
items: Walk-ins welcome without appointment
Most popular choice for foreigners
Affordable fees and short wait times
Recommended for: Common cold, skin issues, minor symptoms

level2.title: 2nd Level (General Hospital)
items: Some departments may require appointments
Often referred from primary clinics
Recommended for: Persistent or severe symptoms, tests, or hospitalization

level3.title: 3rd Level (Tertiary / University Hospital)
items: Handles serious illnesses and advanced treatments
Doctor's referral letter generally required
Appointments essential; long wait times possible
Insurance coverage may be limited without referral
Recommended for: Cancer, major illnesses, surgery, specialized care

walkIn.title: Walk-in (No Appointment Needed)
items: Most primary clinics accept walk-ins
Seen in order of arrival

reservation.title: Appointment Recommended / Required
items: Dermatology, dentistry, orthopedics: Reservations recommended
2nd & 3rd level hospitals: Mostly require appointments
University hospitals: Prior booking usually essential

essential.title: Essential Items
items: Alien Registration Card or Passport
Payment method (cash or card)

additional.title: Additional Items
items: National Health Insurance info or insurance card
Previous medical records, prescriptions, current medications

steps.title: 1) Hospital Visit Steps
items: Present your ID at the reception desk
Briefly describe your symptoms. You can also show Na-um's chart
Your name will be added to the waiting list. Wait for your turn
After consultation, proceed to payment at the billing counter
If you receive a prescription, go to the pharmacy
Submit your prescription at the pharmacy and collect your medication
Always confirm how to take your medication

culture.title: 2) Hospital Culture Differences
items: Consultations may be brief, but this is normal procedure
Answer doctor's questions clearly and concisely
Photography or recording may be restricted inside the hospital

surcharge.title: 1) Additional Fees for Off-Hours Care
items: Night visits cost more than regular daytime visits
Weekends and holidays incur extra charges
Emergency room visits have the highest fees
Surcharge amounts vary by hospital and time

insurance.title: 2) Insurance Coverage Guide

national.title: National Health Insurance Members
items: Pay only a portion of the medical bill
Insurance coverage applied immediately at hospitals

nonNational.title: Non-National Health Insurance Members
items: Must pay full medical costs out-of-pocket
Hospital bills can be significantly higher

private.title: Private Insurance
items: Usually not applied directly at hospitals
Receive receipts and medical records for later reimbursement claims

insurance.note: * Stays of 6 months or longer require enrollment in National Health Insurance

otherTips.title: Other Tips
items: Keep your receipts and medical records
Medical certificates or doctor's notes may incur extra fees
Emergency rooms are the most expensive with long wait times
It's okay to ask the pharmacist again if you're unsure about medication instructions
